headline: South Asia: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen.
- Southern Europe: Ukraine strikes oil facility in St. Petersburg as part of ‘massive’ drone attack.
- Africa: Sudanese gold miners describe deadly airstrike that killed 72.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE

- Politico Europe, The Moscow Times, 10 hours ago: Ukraine strikes oil facility in St. Petersburg as part of ‘massive’ drone attack.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week he had ordered the resumption of strikes on Russian oil refineries following a three-day pause.

Western Russia - bottom line: University lecturer Kostiantyn Chub killed in Russian attack on Poltava.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: University lecturer Kostiantyn Chub killed in Russian attack on Poltava.
Poltava Pedagogical University lecturer Kostiantyn Chub has been killed in a Russian drone attack that targeted residential areas in Poltava.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Warehouse catches fire in Lviv due to Russian drone attack.
A Russian drone attack has damaged a logistics complex and caused a warehouse fire in Malekhiv, while drone debris damaged homes in Murovane.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Russians complain of outages affecting VK social media platform following Ukrainian attack.
Ukrainian FP-1 drones have struck a VK data centre and oil terminals in St Petersburg, triggering service disruptions on VKontakte.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Zelenskyy refutes claims that Russia has captured Dobropillia and advanced towards Zaporizhzhia.
President Zelenskyy has rejected Russian military reports, confirming that Ukrainian forces are holding positions and destroying their units 20 km from Zaporizhzhia.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudanese gold miners describe deadly airstrike that killed 72.
- Africanews, 12 hours ago: Sudanese gold miners describe deadly airstrike that killed 72.
Sudanese miners injured in a deadly airstrike along the border with Egypt last week have been describing how the incident unfolded.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: Nigeria's Army Chief of Staff visits troops in Borno after deaths of 15 soliders.
The Nigerian Army Chief of Staff is visiting troops stationed in the northeast of the country, a few days after jihadists killed fifteen soldiers in the region.
- Africanews, 14 hours ago: DRC accuses ex-president Kabila of planning 'general attack' on the country.
Officials in DR Congo are accusing former president Joseph Kabila of planning a general attack on the country. Kabila on Monday joined forces with the rebel M23 to head a new outfit , taking a more direct role in the insurgency ravaging eastern DRC.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Residents recount drone strikes in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Residents recount drone strikes in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region.
In Adigrat, a city close to the Eritrean border, residents recall recent drone strikes by Ethiopian forces
- Jerusalem Post, 9 hours ago: 'You are the real target': Netanyahu warns Iran developing ICBMs, nuclear weapons to target US.
Netanyahu told FOX News that, if reelected prime minister, his key objectives would be to end the threat posed by Iran, expand the Abraham Accords, and seize the future of AI development.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Sudan army accused of drone strike on livestock market.
Sudan’s army says it struck RSF command centres in South Darfur, but the RSF says a crowded livestock market was hit.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, Taipei Times, Times of India - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, just now: JERUSALEM DAILY: Settlers attack EU diplomats.
Israeli settlers attacked an EU delegation in the occupied West Bank while it was visiting olive harvesters near Taybeh.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen.
Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday. Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said two officers were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the rebel group claimed it shot the aircraft down. The coalition blamed a “technical malfunction” for the helicopter crash, which inflicted its first military fatalities since the long-running conflict with the Houthis reignited in July.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Egypt ‘ready to defend’ Saudi Arabia against Houthis.
• President Sisi says Cairo will take ‘any measure’ to protect kingdom if asked • Iran backs ‘political process’, offers to mediate • Saudi, Houthi forces trade fire CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi pledged on Saturday that Egypt was ready to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi forces if requested, as fighting intensified across the region and Cairo moved towards possible parliamentary authorisation for support.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: 8 India-sponsored terrorists killed in Quetta, Khuzdar, Nushki districts: ISPR.
Security forces have killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during three intelligence-based operations conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday. The IBOs took place on Oct 17 (Saturday) on the “reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxy Fitna al Hindustan”, the military’s media affairs wing said in its press release. The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.
- The Hindu - International, Africanews, Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Drone strikes in the Black Sea raise fears of Russian escalation to test NATO's response.
The attacks in the two countries' exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing. They also run the risk of drawing other countries directly into the war for Ukraine

Palau authorities are investigating an alleged underwater attack by a South Korean divemaster on Taiwanese musician Devon Song and his Bangladeshi divemaster. Song, a member of the music group Nan Quan Mama, posted on social media that he and his divemaster, Sobuj Patwary, were attacked by a South Korean divemaster known as “Romeo”. - South China Morning Post - China, 19 hours ago: How land power could help US forces counter China in the Indo-Pacific.
Senior US commanders have highlighted the importance of land-based troops and equipment stationed in the Asia-Pacific in any conflict with China, countering assumptions that such a war would be fought mainly at sea and in the air. General Ron Clark, commander of US Army Pacific, said the “tyranny of distance” made it difficult to rely on air and naval forces during a panel discussion at the Association of the United States Army’s annual meeting this week. India - bottom line: Manipur in turmoil again: 15 houses torched; 1 killed, several injured in gun attack.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Manipur in turmoil again: 15 houses torched; 1 killed, several injured in gun attack.
In Chassad village, located in Manipur's Kamjong district, at least 15 houses were burned late Saturday night. Suspected militants attacked the village, causing significant chaos and civilians to flee for safety. A Kuki civilian was killed during the assault, and four others suffered injuries from gunfire. Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the violence and called for strict action against the perpetrators.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: Russia sold Alaska for peanuts. Now it guards America against Moscow.
In 1867, Russia sold Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million, reflecting strategic concerns. The decision stemmed from fears of potential conflict with Britain during the Crimean War. Subsequent discoveries of natural resources transformed Alaska's economic importance significantly over the years. Alaska emerged as a crucial military platform for the United States against the Russian Far East.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days if US accepts conditions.
Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi reiterated that the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remains in place. Tehran is analyzing the US response regarding its conditions for ending the conflict. These conditions include lifting sanctions and ending aggression in the region. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a swift resolution to the war and lower gas prices.
